title: Sebastian and the Ledger
premise: When the army requisitions the garrison town of Marrowfield, nurse Wendell Almeida's private ledger — five years of names the officers omitted from casualty reports — is seized as evidence of sedition. Wendell must recover it by allying with Captain Ivo Reyes, once a brother of their found family, now declared an enemy collaborator. As armistice negotiations stall, Wendell discovers the ledger's final page holds proof that could end the war or condemn everyone they love. They keep the peacetime promise to Reyes at devastating personal cost, and the book ends with the armistice signed, the ledger returned to the families of the named, and Wendell finally writing their own true name on the last line.
about_author: Gideon Thackeray is the pen name of a former military archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the paperwork wars leave behind. They write historical fiction about the people history records as margins.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Establishes the infirmary, the ledger hidden beneath floorboards, and the ritual of recording names officers strike from reports. Wendell's found family — cook Bess, orderly Tam, chaplain Odile — gathers for supper. Emotional beat: quiet devotion, the calm before requisition.

chapters.title: Requisition Orders
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Soldiers occupy Marrowfield; a colonel demands all hospital records. Wendell hides the ledger but Tam is caught moving it. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve as the family closes ranks.

chapters.title: What the Colonel Wants
chapters.summary: Colonel Hargreave's POV. He reads seized documents, hunting a leak feeding enemy negotiators. He suspects the infirmary. Emotional beat: cold bureaucratic menace — power that believes itself righteous.

chapters.title: Tam in the Cells
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Tam is interrogated and says nothing, but the ledger's hiding place is compromised. Wendell must move it through occupied streets at night. Emotional beat: guilt and loyalty in collision.

chapters.title: A Face from Peacetime
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Captain Ivo Reyes — once the found family's fifth member, presumed dead — appears in enemy uniform as liaison to the armistice delegation. Emotional beat: shock, joy curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: The Promise
chapters.summary: Flashback, Bess's POV. Three years earlier: Reyes, drunk on leave, asks Wendell to promise that if he's ever declared enemy, they'll hear him out before believing the report. Emotional beat: warmth, and the reader's dread of what the promise will cost.

chapters.title: Declared Enemy
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Official notices brand Reyes a collaborator; Odile urges Wendell to forget him. Wendell secretly leaves a signal only Reyes would know. Emotional beat: divided heart, first act of quiet defiance.

chapters.title: The Signal Answered
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. He sees the signal and risks a midnight meeting, claiming he's a double agent feeding false casualty figures — figures drawn from a ledger he knows exists. Emotional beat: longing and suspicion entwined.

chapters.title: Odile's Doubt
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She suspects Reyes is a plant and warns Wendell that love makes terrible witnesses. Emotional beat: protective friction inside the found family.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Reputation
chapters.summary: Hargreave's POV. Interrogation of Tam yields nothing, but a clerk reports the ledger's existence. Hargreave realizes it documents his own falsified reports. Emotional beat: fear dressed as duty; corruption defending itself.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Bess
chapters.summary: Bess's POV. Hargreave offers Tam's release for information on the ledger's location. Bess stalls him with soup and flattery. Emotional beat: the powerless weaponizing domestic skill.

chapters.title: Night Move
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell smuggles the ledger into the chapel, trusting Odile's sanctuary — not knowing Odile has been ordered to report all hidden papers. Emotional beat: trust as an act of faith with a blade under it.

chapters.title: The Chaplain's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Torn between oath and family, she hides the ledger in the reliquary and lies in her report — her first lie. Emotional beat: conscience cracking open.

chapters.title: Reyes Under Watch
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. His own delegation suspects him; his handler orders him to find the ledger to prove loyalty. Emotional beat: the trap tightening from both sides.

chapters.title: The Infirmary Raid
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Soldiers ransack the infirmary; patients shield Wendell with small lies. The ledger is safe, but Wendell is placed under house arrest. Emotional beat: collective courage of the overlooked.

chapters.title: Letters Not Sent
chapters.summary: Tam's POV, released but broken. He writes to families of the ledger's names and burns the letters he cannot send. Emotional beat: grief given paperwork; why the names matter.

chapters.title: The Armistice Stalls
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Peace talks collapse over casualty figures both sides dispute — figures the ledger could settle or destroy. Emotional beat: history hinging on one hidden book.

chapters.title: Hargreave's Offer
chapters.summary: Hargreave's POV. He offers Wendell freedom and Tam's clean record in exchange for the ledger, framing it as mercy. Emotional beat: corruption speaking the language of kindness.

chapters.title: Wendell Refuses
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell refuses, quoting the ledger's purpose back at him. Hargreave escalates: the infirmary will be closed and staff conscripted to front lines. Emotional beat: fear met with spine.

chapters.title: Bess's Kitchen Conspiracy
chapters.summary: Bess's POV. She organizes the household into a courier network, moving messages between Wendell and Reyes inside bread loaves. Emotional beat: found family as infrastructure of resistance.

chapters.title: The Reliquary Empty
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell retrieves the ledger and finds the reliquary watched; Odile covers with a staged prayer service. Emotional beat: terror and gratitude; the family now complicit together.

chapters.title: Reyes's Gamble
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. He falsifies a search report to buy time, knowing discovery means execution. Emotional beat: love justifying treason.

chapters.title: What the Last Page Says
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell rereads the ledger and realizes the final entry names Hargreave's own son among the omitted dead — the one name Hargreave cannot survive being public. Emotional beat: revelation that power's weakness is its grief.

chapters.title: Odile's Sermon
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She preaches on names and forgetting before a congregation including officers, a coded warning that the truth will surface. Emotional beat: moral courage in liturgy.

chapters.title: The Betrayal
chapters.summary: A young clerk's POV. Terrified, he reports the chapel hiding place to save his brother from conscription. Emotional beat: betrayal born of the same love that drives loyalty.

chapters.title: Chapel Sealed
chapters.summary: Hargreave's POV. He orders the chapel searched at dawn; the ledger is gone — moved hours earlier by Bess. He arrests Odile instead. Emotional beat: fury of a man chasing a book through other people's bodies.

chapters.title: Odile in Custody
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Interrogated, she refuses to confirm anything, finding strength in ritual and scripture. Emotional beat: serenity as resistance.

chapters.title: The Exchange Proposed
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. He proposes to his handler a trade: the ledger for Odile and the stalled talks. He is authorized — because his handler wants the ledger too. Emotional beat: walking into a trap with eyes open.

chapters.title: Wendell's Decision
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Weighing the promise to Reyes against the ledger's safety, Wendell chooses both: bring the ledger, keep the promise, trust the found family to cover the escape. Emotional beat: resolve; the theme of identity — deciding who one is by what one risks.

chapters.title: The Mill Meeting
chapters.summary: Wendell's and Reyes's alternating POV. The exchange at the abandoned mill; both delegations have hidden soldiers. Emotional beat: dread rising toward the breaking point.

chapters.title: Ambush
chapters.summary: Hargreave's POV. He springs his own trap, intending to seize the ledger and execute Reyes as a traitor to both sides. Shots; Tam is wounded shielding Wendell. Emotional beat: chaos, the cost made flesh.

chapters.title: Burning the Mill Road
chapters.summary: Bess's POV. She drives the cart, decoys the pursuit, and gets Wendell and the ledger out through the marsh. Emotional beat: ferocious maternal courage.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. In hiding, Wendell reads the ledger aloud to Reyes, name by name — including Hargreave's son. Emotional beat: grief shared across enemy lines; the ledger becomes a litany.

chapters.title: Reyes's Choice
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. He decides to deliver the ledger to the armistice table itself, not his handlers, forcing both delegations to confront the true count. Emotional beat: treason transfigured into testimony.

chapters.title: Hargreave's Son
chapters.summary: Hargreave's POV. Confronted privately by Wendell with his son's name and the circumstances of his omitted death, Hargreave breaks. Emotional beat: power's corruption meeting its mirror — a father's grief.

chapters.title: The Armistice Table
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. The ledger is read into the record; casualty figures are corrected; the armistice is signed by dawn. Emotional beat: catharsis — the names doing what armies could not.

chapters.title: Prices Paid
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Odile is released; Tam survives, changed; the clerk's brother is spared; Reyes faces a tribunal but the record now defends him. Emotional beat: bittersweet accounting.

chapters.title: Returning the Names
chapters.summary: Bess's POV. The family copies the ledger and delivers entries to families across the region, watching strangers weep over a line of ink. Emotional beat: restoration, name by name.

chapters.title: The Tribunal
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Cleared on the strength of the armistice record, Reyes chooses exile from the army rather than promotion within it. Emotional beat: refusing corrupted power even when it offers reward.

chapters.title: The Last Line
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The found family reunites in a rebuilt infirmary; Wendell writes a final entry — their own birth name, long abandoned, and the words 'kept safe.' Emotional beat: identity reclaimed; the ledger closed and begun again.
